newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day peso ends in tailspin on jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day peso ends in tailspin on jitters.

text.p: Mexico's same-day peso closed 11.65 centavos weaker at 7.9250/7.9300 per dollar on Friday, as dollars were made scarce by foreign investors bailing out of Mexico and local speculation abounded over the "pacto", traders said.

"What we're seeing is outright speculation...every one has their own excuse, be it Dornbusch, the pacto, U.S. presidential elections, or whatever," a trader said. He referred to U.S. economist Rudiger Dornbusch, who has said the peso needs to weaken.

The still-trading benchmark 48-hour and 24-hour peso contracts were meanwhile 8.05 and 8.75 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9500/7.525 and 7.9250/7.9450 per dollar. The same-day peso weakened more than its counterparts, as it had lagged behind market weakness in late trade on Thursday.
The "pacto" is a three-way agreement between government, business and labor leaders designed to set wage hikes and control inflation in the year ahead
Jitters in the foreign exchange market have tended to follow comments in the local press by Dornbusch, a leading critic of Mexican policy towards the peso.
